```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(forcats)
```

## Step 0: Load and Clean Data

```{r load-data}
# 311 cases only. (The evictions dataset and install.packages() were removed:
# install.packages() should be run once in the console, not inside a knitted file.)
url <- "https://data.sfgov.org/resource/vw6y-z8j6.json?$limit=5000"

df <- fromJSON(url)

# View(df)   # keep View() out of the knitted file, run it in the console instead
names(df)
```

```{r hours-to-close}
# Hours to close
cases <- df %>%
  # nested columns (e.g. "point") come in as data frames and break later steps
  select(-where(is.data.frame)) %>%
  mutate(
    opened = as.POSIXct(requested_datetime,
                        format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS"),
    closed = as.POSIXct(closed_date,
                        format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS"),
    hours_to_close = as.numeric(
      difftime(closed, opened, units = "hours")
    ),
    lat  = as.numeric(lat),    # JSON delivers these as text
    long = as.numeric(long)
  )

summary(cases$hours_to_close)
```

```{r cleaning}
# DATA CLEANING: Remove invalid closure times
# We found 9 cases with negative closure times (closed before opened).
# Remove these observations because closure time cannot be negative.
# Also remove cases with missing closure times.
# Keep the original dataset unchanged by creating a cleaned dataset.

# (cases_clean must be created BEFORE we compute anything on it)
cases_clean <- cases[
  !is.na(cases$hours_to_close) &
  cases$hours_to_close >= 0,
]

# Verify that no negative closure times remain
sum(cases_clean$hours_to_close < 0)

# Check the number of observations remaining after cleaning
nrow(cases_clean)

# DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS: Outcome variable (Y)
# Calculate the mean, median, standard deviation,
# minimum, maximum, and quartiles of closure time.

summary(cases_clean$hours_to_close)
sd(cases_clean$hours_to_close, na.rm = TRUE)

# Date range of the data (tells us whether season is usable, and whether
# we are looking at one year or several)
range(cases_clean$opened)
```

```{r minutes}
# Use minutes to close a request as output instead?
# Minutes vs hours is only a change of units (x60). It does not change the
# shape of the distribution, the model fit, or which predictors matter.
# It only changes how coefficients are read ("minutes" vs "hours").
# Minutes are only useful if a large share of cases close within an hour.

cases_clean <- cases_clean %>%
  mutate(
    minutes_to_close = hours_to_close * 60,
    log_hours = log1p(hours_to_close)    # log(1 + hours): handles zeros, tames skew
  )

mean(cases_clean$hours_to_close < 1)     # share closed in under 1 hour
mean(cases_clean$hours_to_close < 24)    # share closed in under 1 day
quantile(cases_clean$hours_to_close, c(.05, .25, .5, .75, .9, .95, .99))
```

#### Missing Values

```{r missing}
is_missing <- function(x) {
  if (is.character(x)) is.na(x) | x == "" else is.na(x)
}

cases_model <- cases_clean %>%
  select(any_of(c(
    "hours_to_close", "log_hours", "opened",
    "agency_responsible", "agency_c",
    "service_name", "service_subtype",
    "analysis_neighborhood", "neighborhood_c",
    "police_district", "supervisor_district",
    "source", "lat", "long"
  )))

# Which columns actually made it into cases_model?
names(cases_model)

# Missing values per column
missing_model <- data.frame(
  variable    = names(cases_model),
  type        = sapply(cases_model, function(x) class(x)[1]),
  n_missing   = sapply(cases_model, function(x) sum(is_missing(x))),
  pct_missing = round(100 * sapply(cases_model, function(x) mean(is_missing(x))), 1),
  n_unique    = sapply(cases_model, n_distinct),
  row.names   = NULL
) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

missing_model

# How many rows survive if we drop every row with any missing value?
nrow(cases_model)
nrow(na.omit(cases_model))
```

###

```{r categorical}
# Categorical variables in cases_model: how many levels, which levels,
# and which are too sparse to estimate in a regression.

# Treat blank strings as missing so they are visible in the counts
cases_model <- cases_model %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "")))

is_cat <- function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x)

# 1. How many distinct values does each categorical column have?
cat_summary <- cases_model %>%
  select(where(is_cat)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_unique") %>%
  arrange(n_unique)
cat_summary

# 2. For columns with a manageable number of levels, list levels and counts
small_cats <- cat_summary %>% filter(n_unique <= 30) %>% pull(variable)

for (v in small_cats) {
  cat("\n====", v, "====\n")
  print(sort(table(cases_model[[v]], useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE))
}

# 3. Sparse levels (fewer than 10 cases) and dummy-column cost per variable
sparse_check <- lapply(cat_summary$variable, function(v) {
  tab <- table(cases_model[[v]])
  data.frame(
    variable        = v,
    n_levels        = length(tab),
    dummy_columns   = length(tab) - 1,          # k - 1 parameters in a regression
    levels_under_10 = sum(tab < 10),
    pct_in_top5     = round(100 * sum(sort(tab, decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(5, length(tab))]) / sum(tab), 1)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(desc(dummy_columns))
sparse_check
```



```{r collapse-example}
# Keep levels with at least 20 cases, lump the rest into "Other"
cases_clean <- cases_clean %>%
  mutate(
    neighborhood_c = fct_lump_min(factor(analysis_neighborhood), min = 20,
                                  other_level = "Other"),
    agency_c       = fct_lump_min(factor(agency_responsible), min = 20,
                                  other_level = "Other")
  )
table(cases_clean$neighborhood_c)
table(cases_clean$agency_c)
```

## Plots

```{r outcome-plots, echo=FALSE}
# Outcome variable: show me hours
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(cases_clean$hours_to_close, breaks = 50, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
     main = "Hours to close (raw)", xlab = "Hours")
hist(cases_clean$log_hours, breaks = 40, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
     main = "log(1 + hours)", xlab = "log(1 + hours)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Zoomed view of the raw scale: first 7 days only
cases_clean %>%
  filter(hours_to_close <= 24 * 7) %>%
  ggplot(aes(hours_to_close)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 6, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(x = "Hours to close (cases closed within 7 days)", y = "Cases")
```

## Plots

```{r plot-setup, include=FALSE}
# Run this chunk first: shared theme, axis labels, and the plotting data.
# Uses cases_model (needs: opened, hours_to_close, log_hours, police_district,
# analysis_neighborhood, lat, long). Swap in cases_clean if any are missing.

library(scales)

# hours + 1 lets us use a log axis even when a case closes in 0 hours
plot_df <- cases_model %>% mutate(h1 = hours_to_close + 1)

# Readable axis: ticks in hours / days / weeks instead of log numbers
hrs_at     <- c(0, 1, 6, 24, 72, 168, 720)
hrs_labels <- c("0", "1 hr", "6 hrs", "1 day", "3 days", "1 week", "1 month")
x_hours <- scale_x_log10(breaks = hrs_at + 1, labels = hrs_labels)
y_hours <- scale_y_log10(breaks = hrs_at + 1, labels = hrs_labels)

theme_311 <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "grey35"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
theme_set(theme_311)

col_main <- "#2C7FB8"
```

### Outcome distribution

```{r outcome-plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
share_1h  <- mean(plot_df$hours_to_close < 1)
share_24h <- mean(plot_df$hours_to_close < 24)
med_h     <- median(plot_df$hours_to_close)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(h1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 45, fill = col_main, color = "white", linewidth = .2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_h + 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey25") +
  annotate("text", x = med_h + 1, y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.1, size = 3.8,
           label = paste0("Median: ", round(med_h, 1), " hrs")) +
  x_hours +
  labs(title = "Most 311 cases close within a day or two",
       subtitle = paste0(percent(share_1h, .1), " close within 1 hour; ",
                         percent(share_24h, .1), " within 24 hours"),
       x = "Time to close (log scale)", y = "Number of cases")
```

### Time series

```{r time-series, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# Monthly median closure time per police district, one panel per district.
# The grey line is the citywide median so each district can be compared to it.
# Months with fewer than 5 cases are dropped (too noisy).

ts_district <- plot_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(police_district)) %>%
  mutate(open_month = floor_date(opened, "month")) %>%
  group_by(open_month, police_district) %>%
  summarise(med = median(h1), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 5)

ts_city <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(open_month = floor_date(opened, "month")) %>%
  group_by(open_month) %>%
  summarise(med = median(h1), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(ts_district, aes(open_month, med)) +
  geom_line(data = ts_city, color = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(color = col_main, linewidth = .9) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), color = col_main, alpha = .7) +
  facet_wrap(~ police_district) +
  y_hours +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 4)) +
  labs(title = "Median closure time over time, by police district",
       subtitle = "Blue: district median. Grey: citywide median. Point size = cases that month.",
       x = NULL, y = "Median time to close", size = "Cases")
```

```{r weekly-volume, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
plot_df %>%
  count(week = floor_date(opened, "week")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(week, n)) +
  geom_area(fill = col_main, alpha = .25) +
  geom_line(color = col_main, linewidth = .9) +
  labs(title = "Weekly case volume", x = NULL, y = "Cases opened")
```

```{r censoring-check, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
# Do closure times fall at the end of the range? (open cases were dropped,
# so recent cases only appear if they closed quickly)
plot_df %>%
  group_by(open_month = floor_date(opened, "month")) %>%
  summarise(Median = median(h1),
            `90th percentile` = quantile(h1, .9),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 5) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Median, `90th percentile`)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(open_month, value, color = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  y_hours +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Median = col_main, `90th percentile` = "#D95F0E")) +
  labs(title = "Censoring check: does closure time drop in the latest months?",
       subtitle = "A sharp fall at the right edge means recent slow cases are still open (and missing)",
       x = "Month opened", y = "Time to close", color = NULL)
```

### Map

```{r map, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
geo <- plot_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(long), lat != 0, long != 0) %>%
  arrange(h1)   # draw the slowest cases last so they stay visible

ggplot(geo, aes(long, lat, color = h1)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .75, size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1, trans = "log10",
                        breaks = hrs_at[-1] + 1, labels = hrs_labels[-1],
                        name = "Time to close") +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(title = "Where are the slow cases?",
       subtitle = "Each point is one closed 311 case") +
  theme_void(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey35"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"))
```

```{r map-district, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
geo %>% filter(!is.na(police_district)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(long, lat, color = police_district)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .8, size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo", name = NULL) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(title = "Cases by police district") +
  theme_void(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Closure time by group (one reusable function)

```{r box-fn}
# Horizontal boxplots ordered by median, box color = group median,
# n in each label, dashed line = overall median, groups with < min_n cases hidden.
box_by <- function(data, var, min_n = 10, top_n = 20, title = NULL) {
  d <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>%
    group_by(grp = as.character(.data[[var]])) %>%
    mutate(n = n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(n >= min_n)

  keep <- d %>% count(grp, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = top_n) %>% pull(grp)

  d <- d %>%
    filter(grp %in% keep) %>%
    mutate(lab = paste0(stringr::str_trunc(grp, 35), "  (n=", n, ")"),
           lab = fct_reorder(lab, h1, median)) %>%
    group_by(lab) %>% mutate(med = median(h1)) %>% ungroup()

  ggplot(d, aes(h1, lab, fill = med)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .8, outlier.alpha = .3, linewidth = .4, alpha = .9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = median(d$h1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = hrs_at + 1, labels = hrs_labels) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "log10", guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = paste0("Groups with at least ", min_n,
                           " cases. Dashed line = overall median."),
         x = "Time to close (log scale)", y = NULL)
}
```

```{r box-neighborhood, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
box_by(plot_df, "analysis_neighborhood", min_n = 10, top_n = 25,
       title = "Closure time by neighborhood")
```

The agency responsible for fulfilling or otherwise addressing the service request.

```{r box-district, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
       title = "Closure time by police district")
```
